issues.note: Example models the 'Although ..., but ...' error the entry itself forbids.
False origin: although is all + though, not Latin alter.
Plain if is not a real confusable of although; it has no note.
When is not a typical confusable here; no note explains the link.
Register reversed: though is more informal and spoken, although more formal.
Clause order is the same; 'in the other order' misleads learners.
The no-but rule appears in three fields, against one fact, one field.
Ungrammatical example a learner could copy; same problem as issue 1.

findings.F1: Sense 1 example uses 'Although ..., but ...', the very error the entry warns against
findings.F2: Etymology falsely derives although from Latin alter through French
findings.F3: Synonym discrimination reverses the register of although and though
findings.F4: if-conj listed as a compare item without being a real confusable
findings.F5: when-conj listed as a compare item without being a real confusable
findings.F6: but-conj compare note wrongly says but puts the ideas in the other order
findings.F7: The rule against using although with but is repeated in explanation, adaptation note, and learner error
